bills.title: AI Communications Privilege
bills.summary: Would establish that user communications with AI are privileged if such communication would be privileged if sought from a human professional.

bills.title: Surveillance Pricing Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit surveillance pricing unless certain criteria are met.

bills.title: Chatbot Identity Disclosure
bills.summary: Would prohibit chatbots from misleading a person about their artificial identity to incentivize the purchase or sale of goods or services.

bills.title: Florida AI Bill of Rights
bills.summary: Would provide citizens certain AI rights, including the right to limit minors' access to AI and to know if AI companies collect personal information. Requires notice for chatbots and prohibits entities from providing licensed therapy or mental health counseling through AI.
bills.status_detail: Reported favorably out of first committee on January 21, 2026

bills.title: Chatbot Litigation Confidentiality
bills.summary: Would prevent certain information pertaining to chatbot litigation from being made public until the completion of an investigation.
bills.status_detail: Reported favorably out of committee on January 21, 2026

bills.title: Healthcare AI Disclosure and Oversight
bills.summary: Would require health care providers using AI to disclose their use to patients. Providers would also be required to hire AI oversight personnel to oversee the use of AI in the healthcare context.

bills.title: Chatbot Safety for Minors
bills.summary: Chatbot safety bill addressing protections for minors. Passed policy committee on January 15, 2026 and set to be heard in Appropriations on January 22, 2026.
bills.status_detail: Passed policy committee on January 15, 2026; set for Appropriations hearing January 22, 2026

bills.title: Comprehensive Privacy and AI Transparency Act
bills.summary: Comprehensive privacy bill that would apply to any company processing personal data of at least 5,000 Iowa residents annually. Companies would be required to post privacy notices, obtain consent prior to processing personal data, and comply with individual rights of access, correction, and deletion. Also requires disclosures for data used in automated decision making or AI training. Includes a private right of action.

bills.title: Chatbot Age Verification for Minors
bills.summary: Would prohibit chatbots from being made available to minors if they have human-like features and would require the implementation of reasonable age-verification systems.

bills.title: Chatbot Restrictions for Minors
bills.summary: Would prohibit chatbots with human-like features from being made available to minors. Similar to Maine LD 2162.

bills.title: AI in Mental and Behavioral Health Care
bills.summary: Illinois HB 1806-style bill that would set restrictions on the use of AI in mental or behavioral health care.

bills.title: AI Definition in Mississippi Code
bills.summary: Would define artificial intelligence in Mississippi code.

bills.title: AI Fraud Liability
bills.summary: Would allow any entity damaged by AI fraud to seek compensatory or statutory damages. Any entity that knowingly develops, deploys, or facilitates AI systems for fraudulent behavior would be held liable.

bills.title: Frontier Model and Chatbot Child Safety
bills.summary: Combines California SB 53-style definitions of frontier models and catastrophic risk with child safety and chatbot-related requirements. Would require large frontier model developers and large chatbot providers to develop and publish a public safety and child protection plan, including processes to assess and manage catastrophic risk. An identical bill was introduced in Utah as HB 286.

bills.title: Chatbot Transparency and Minor Protections
bills.summary: Mandates disclosures to minors when they are conversing with chatbots, requires implementation of safety protocols, and requires privacy and account management functions for the parents of minor users.

bills.title: AI Employment Regulation
bills.summary: Employment-related AI bill. Reported favorably out of the Assembly Science and Technology Committee on January 21, 2026.
bills.status_detail: Reported favorably out of Assembly Science and Technology Committee on January 21, 2026

bills.title: RAISE Act Governor's Amendments
bills.summary: Governor's amendments to the RAISE Act. Reported favorably out of the Assembly Science and Technology Committee on January 21, 2026.
bills.status_detail: Reported favorably out of Assembly Science and Technology Committee on January 21, 2026

bills.title: Oklahoma AI Bill of Rights
bills.summary: Florida AI Bill of Rights-style bill with similar requirements for government use of AI, NIL protections, parental controls for minors, and deidentification requirements. Does not include restrictions on AI providing advice reserved for licensed professionals such as therapists.

bills.title: Food Retail Algorithmic Pricing Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit all food retail establishments from using personalized algorithmic pricing or surveillance pricing. Includes a private right of action.

bills.title: AI Prohibitions in Life-or-Death and Employment Contexts
bills.summary: Would prohibit the use of AI in life and death situations or to replace workers.

bills.title: Chatbot Protections for Minors and Therapeutic Use
bills.summary: Would establish protections for minors and requirements for therapeutic chatbot use.

bills.title: AI in Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: Illinois HB 1806-style bill that would set restrictions on the use of AI in health care.

bills.title: CHAT Act State Replica — Chatbot Safety for Minors
bills.summary: Would replicate the federal CHAT Act, imposing specific safety requirements, mandating disclaimers, and requiring explicit consent for training AI models with minors' data.

bills.title: Frontier Model and Chatbot Child Safety
bills.summary: Combines California SB 53-style definitions of frontier models and catastrophic risk with child safety and chatbot-related requirements. Identical to Nebraska LB 1083 introduced the same week.

bills.title: Generative AI Provenance Data Requirements
bills.summary: Would establish provenance data requirements for generative AI.

bills.title: Expanding Healthcare Practitioners' AI Use
bills.summary: Would expand healthcare practitioners' ability to use AI.

bills.title: Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure Requirements
bills.summary: Would establish disclosure requirements for algorithmic pricing.

bills.title: AI Transparency Act (California-style)
bills.summary: California AI Transparency Act-style bill requiring disclosure and transparency for AI systems. Passed committee on January 14, 2026.

bills.title: Generative AI Training Data Transparency
bills.summary: Based on California AB 2013, would require generative AI providers to publish certain information regarding data used to train their systems.

bills.title: High-Risk AI Systems Requirements (CAIA-style)
bills.summary: CAIA-style bill introduced by a bipartisan group of Senators that would impose requirements on deployers of high-risk AI systems. Unlike the Colorado AI Act, contains no developer requirements.

bills.title: AI in Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: Identical to Illinois HB 1806, setting restrictions on the use of AI in health care.

bills.title: AI-Generated Media Disclosure
bills.summary: Would require disclosures when media is generated or altered by AI.

bills.title: Federal Agency Civil Rights Offices for AI Bias
bills.summary: Would require agencies that use, fund, or oversee algorithms to establish an office of Civil Rights focused on bias, discrimination, and other harms. Introduced by Sen. Markey (D-MA) and Rep. Lee (D-PA).
bills.status_detail: Introduced; no bill text yet available

bills.title: Federal Agency Civil Rights Offices for AI Bias (House)
bills.summary: House companion to S 3680. Would require agencies that use, fund, or oversee algorithms to establish an office of Civil Rights focused on bias, discrimination, and other harms. Introduced by Rep. Lee (D-PA) and Sen. Markey (D-MA).
bills.status_detail: Introduced; no bill text yet available

bills.title: App Store Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Would establish an App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework with requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and no application exemptions.

bills.title: Biological and Neural Data Privacy
bills.summary: Would prohibit the disclosure of biological data or neural data without a consumer's consent. Biological data includes data generated by measurement of an individual's biological, genetic, biochemical, physiological, or neural properties used for identification purposes.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act
bills.summary: Alabama App Store Accountability Act bill. The Alabama House unanimously passed the bill on January 22, 2026, moving it to the Senate for further consideration.
bills.status_detail: Passed Alabama House unanimously on January 22, 2026; sent to Senate

bills.title: Illinois Comprehensive Privacy Act (Minnesota-style)
bills.summary: Minnesota-style comprehensive privacy bill with numerical applicability thresholds and a small business exemption. Includes a specific geolocation data definition based on decimal coordinates, requires controllers to maintain a data inventory as part of security obligations, and provides a right to contest adverse profiling decisions.

bills.title: Genetic Information Privacy Act Amendment — Insurance
bills.summary: Would amend Illinois's Genetic Information Privacy Act to limit the use of genetic testing information in insurance.

bills.title: Genetic Information Privacy Act Amendment — Biomarkers
bills.summary: Would amend Illinois's Genetic Information Privacy Act to expand protections to include biomarkers and biomarker testing. Biomarker is defined as a characteristic objectively measured as an indicator of normal biological processes, pathogenic processes, or pharmacologic responses, including gene mutations or protein expression.

bills.title: Data-Driven Pricing Regulation
bills.summary: Data-driven pricing bill cited as recently active in the 2026 legislative session.

bills.title: Mississippi Comprehensive Privacy Act (Tennessee-style)
bills.summary: Tennessee-style comprehensive privacy bill with heightened applicability thresholds including a minimum revenue requirement, a broad pseudonymous data carve-out with respect to consumer rights, and a safe harbor for controllers that comply with the NIST privacy framework. Includes a narrow definition of biometric data that excludes data generated from photos and videos and information irreversibly converted to a mathematical representation.

bills.title: Nebraska AADC Amendment
bills.summary: Would amend Nebraska's Age-Appropriate Design Code to broaden the definition of covered online service, expand the definition of covered design features, restrict services from providing a single setting that reduces all default privacy settings, and require services to provide an accessible tool allowing minors to delete their accounts.

bills.title: NJDPA Amendment — New Exemptions
bills.summary: Holdover from 2024-25 legislative session amending the New Jersey Data Privacy Act. Adds new exemptions for insurance-support organizations, HIPAA-treated health information, human subjects research, and national securities associations. Also expands the definition of deidentified data to include HIPAA-deidentified data. Approved January 20, 2026; takes effect immediately.
bills.status_detail: Approved (enacted) on January 20, 2026; takes effect immediately

bills.title: Community and Health Information Safety and Privacy Act
bills.summary: Novel comprehensive privacy bill regulating the collection and use of personal data by broadly-defined covered entities. Would require default privacy settings to be most protective, provide privacy notice, comply with consumer rights, and maintain data security. Includes distinct default protections for minors, default prohibitions on profiling and processing beyond service necessity, and prohibitions on geofencing health care or immigration services. Includes a private right of action.

bills.title: New York Governor's Budget — Privacy and Safety Provisions (Senate)
bills.summary: Governor's budget proposal in the Senate including a Data Broker Accountability Act modeled on California's Delete Act establishing a data broker registry and mass deletion mechanism, and a Safety by Design Act requiring age assurance for online platforms with minor audiences, specific privacy defaults for minors, and parental tools for transaction limits.
bills.status_detail: Introduced as part of Governor's budget proposal

bills.title: New York Governor's Budget — Privacy and Safety Provisions (Assembly)
bills.summary: Governor's budget proposal in the Assembly including a Data Broker Accountability Act modeled on California's Delete Act establishing a data broker registry and mass deletion mechanism, and a Safety by Design Act requiring age assurance for online platforms with minor audiences, specific privacy defaults for minors, and parental tools for transaction limits.
bills.status_detail: Introduced as part of Governor's budget proposal

bills.title: South Carolina Age-Appropriate Design Code
bills.summary: Age-Appropriate Design Code bill. On January 21, 2026, the Senate concurred to House amendments and approved the measure for ratification. Once ratified and transmitted to Governor McMaster, he will have 5 days to sign or veto.
bills.status_detail: Senate concurred to House amendments and approved for ratification on January 21, 2026; awaiting governor action

bills.title: VCDPA Amendment — Minor Protections and Duty of Care
bills.summary: Would amend the Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act to add a heightened access right for minors under 18, prohibit controllers from entering into user agreements with minors without verifiable parental consent, add disclosure requirements for advertising directed at minors, and establish a duty of care to prevent harms including self-harm, bullying, harassment, sexual exploitation, and predatory marketing.

bills.title: VCDPA Amendment — Geolocation Data Sale Prohibition
bills.summary: Would amend the Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act to prohibit a controller from selling precise geolocation data.

bills.title: VCDPA Amendment — Data-Driven Pricing Prohibition
bills.summary: Would amend the Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act to prohibit a controller or processor from generating a price offered to a consumer through their online device based on device hardware or state, software presence, or precise geolocation data used to make inferences about the consumer. Subject to exceptions.

bills.title: VCDPA Amendment — Social Media Private Right of Action
bills.summary: Would amend the Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act to add a private right of action against social media platforms, subject to a cure requirement.
